equation_request.abstract: We investigate the graph isomorphism (GI) in some cospectral networks. Two graph are isomorphic when they are related to each other by a relabeling of the graph vertices. We want to investigate the GI in two scalable (n + 2)-regular graphs $G_{4}(n;n+2)$ and $G_{5}(n;n+2)$, analytically by using the multiparticle quantum walk. These two graphs are a pair of non-isomorphic connected cospectral regular graphs for any positive integer $n$. In order to investigation GI in these two graphs, we rewrite the adjacency matrices of graphs in the antisymmetric fermionic basis and show that they are different for these pairs of graphs. So the multiparticle quantum walk is able to distinguish pairs of non-isomorph graphs. Also we construct two new graphs $T_{4}(n;n+2)$ and $T_{5}(n;n+2)$ and repeat the same process of $G_{4}$ and $G_{5}$ to study the GI problem by using multiparticle quantum walk. Then we study GI by using the entanglement entropy. To this aim, we calculate entanglement entropy between two parts of network. In our model the nodes are considered as identical quantum harmonic oscillators. The entanglement entropy between two special parts of $G_{4}(n;n+2)$ and $G_{5}(n;n+2)$ are calculated analytically. It is shown that the entanglement entropy can distinguish pairs of non-isomorphic cospectral graphs too.

specification.problem: Distinguish non-isomorphic cospectral regular graphs G4(n;n+2) and G5(n;n+2), and the derived T4, T5, via multiparticle (fermionic) quantum walk adjacency matrices and via entanglement entropy between two parts of a network of identical quantum harmonic oscillators.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Theoretical graph-isomorphism analysis (analytic, not a circuit experiment); reconstruct only the formal setup that the abstract supports. Explicit graph constructions and entropy results are not in the abstract.

specification.initial_state: Not specified in abstract; assumed an antisymmetrized fermionic multiparticle vertex state, or oscillator ground state for the entropy part.

steps.description: Build the adjacency matrices of G4 and G5 (and T4, T5) and confirm they are cospectral for the single-particle walk.
Rewrite the adjacency matrices in the antisymmetric fermionic multiparticle basis and compare them between the two graphs.
Model nodes as coupled identical harmonic oscillators, partition the network into two parts, and compute the entanglement entropy of the reduced state.

specification.measurement: No physical measurement is specified; the analysis is analytic. Graphs are distinguished by comparing the multiparticle (fermionic-basis) adjacency matrices or spectra of G4 vs G5 (and T4 vs T5), and by comparing the entanglement entropy S between two parts of each network.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Compare the fermionic-basis adjacency matrices/spectra and the entropy values for each graph pair; differing results indicate non-isomorphism. No numerical procedure is given in the abstract.
